sources_considered.why: Quotes Ilya Sutskever, OpenAI's former chief scientist, calling 2020–2025 the 'age of scaling' and explaining why companies invested in it.
Independent measurement of training compute growth and how much of the progress came from scale.
Primary US policy document that treats AI compute as essential.
Stargate investment context. Not read; the Action Plan and the Sutskever account already cover policy and investment.

receipt.public_excerpt: Now, from 2020 to 2025, it was the age of scaling—maybe plus or minus, let’s add error bars to those years—because people say, ‘This is amazing. You’ve got to scale more. Keep scaling.’ The one word: scaling.”

evidence_items.explanation: A central figure in the scaling approach describes 2020–2025 as the 'age of scaling'. This matches Marcus's 'last half decade' of dominance in research.

receipt.public_excerpt: Companies love this because it gives you a very low-risk way of investing your resources. It’s much harder to invest your resources in research.

evidence_items.explanation: Sutskever says scaling shaped how companies invested their resources. This backs the investment part of the claim.

receipt.public_excerpt: we estimate that about two-thirds of the improvements in performance in language models in the last decade have been due to increases in model scale.

evidence_items.explanation: An independent research group finds that scaling was the main source of language model progress. The same report finds training compute grew 4-5x a year.
